questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an english speaking country, to improve my english and to have a different experience to my first exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, they gave you a lot of information (maybe even too much) but they were super helpfull if you had any questions

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was shown to my accommodation (they even had an airport shuttle service, but i did not use this). They also gave you a free welcome package with sim card, snacks and info about the uni. I also got a lot of help with getting my modules right, as this ended up being a bit tricky.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many different dorms or shared housing

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You could get catering but I didn't do this as we had a perfectly fine kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That there most likely will be nothing in the house except for the furniture. We had to go buy duvets, kitchen equipment and many other things...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied because it was so easy and i was never worried about where to live, but it was a bit troublesome having to get all of this stuff...

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Just a website where you fill out some things..

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Wasn't needed as it was simple, but im sure you could contact them

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got maybe half of them.. a combination of KU not approving my classes and the classes overlapping meaning that Uni of leeds did not allow me to take them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: if there is one course in particular that you want, be quick and maybe even write to the school as they can fill up in some cases.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Would say a lower level than UCPH for both BA and MA. But they care a lot about academic writing!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Understanding data for decision making
- New venture creation
- Artificial Intelligence
- Forensic accounting and finance
- Economic institutions (Labour)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Forensic accounting and finance was really interesting and the professor was very good and passionate about it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Buying all the stuff for the house was a bit unexpected (at least that it was so many things missing..)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Trains were more expensive than i thought they would be, so travelling around in the UK became more expensive...
But Leeds is generally cheaper than Copenhagen!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Any thing you could dream of! There is a society for everything!!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I joined the Book club which was so nice, they did book discussions and other socials. The art society is also so good! They do a lot of life drawing events and other fun things. Would also really recommend joining some sort of sports society as they have a lot of events and are a great way of meeting people. My roommate was in the handball society and he made a lot of really good friends there!
For all societies any level is welcome so it's a great opportunity to try something new!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go hiking! You can join the hiking society but their entry fee is a lot. Otherwise go with GOGA that is cheaper. Or find someone to go with and plan it yourself there are so many beautiful spots nearby!!!
Would also recommend going to York, Harrogate, Manchester, Bristol and Edinburgh!
And my favourite place was definitely Saltaire which is really close to Leeds. The old Salts mill there is a big David Hockney museum and it is so beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy as it is similar to denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Not challenging just very different: they seem immune to the cold and never wear coats even in the cold winter months...
And maybe a bit the fact that they are all very young when they go to uni, but i quickly adjusted :-)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Pub culture! I love that you can just go for a beer and a game of pool or have your sunday roast there. The pubs are in even the smallest villages and it is always such a warm and welcome space!!!
Also! There is so much live music. Hyde park book club does jazz every thursday and going there was my favourite tradition through the semester

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Living in shared housing was so nice, and probably the most value for money compared to the accommodation that some of my friends were in. 
You can rent a bike for very cheap through uni! Leeds is not the most bike friendly city though... But nice if you are a bike loving dane :-)
Have fun and enjoy your semester!! :-)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: We had a month long break around easter which i didn't really know before going.. a lot of people travel in this period of time. I would recommend doing the same or planning your friends/family visiting in this time as the city becomes a bit more quiet.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living with people from all over the world. Having roomies from singapore, south korea, france and germany meant that we had some really interesting conversations and i learned a lot from them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Arriving in winter was quite hard as people are just not out as much and it was cold and dark.. Luckily the uni did a lot of events and made it more fun :-)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
